_comment: Per-week progress reports for the Gantt detail panel. Hand-edit this file. Keys are week numbers (strings) matching the Gantt's W0..W12. Each week has three sections: planned (set at the start of the week), refactored (mid-week scope changes / re-plans), accomplished (what actually got done). Items are plain strings, or { name, status } where status is 'todo' | 'done'.

4.label: MVP Phase 1 — Music Genre (BEARDOWN)
planned: EDA + standalone site design — Music Genre
Music Genre experimental design [a, b, c]
Standalone site: run sweeps, model lock, drop-in analysis
refactored: Genre became the reference implementation: the full BEARDOWN-depth treatment here defines the standalone-site template that phonon (W5) and ATLAS (W6) copy — so genre absorbed extra build time up front to de-risk models 2 and 3.

“Min. Bayesian options (LLLA + HMC)” split into two stages: W4 staged the bundle for it (cached phi_train.npy + ggn_eig.npz so the head is plug-ready); the LLLA/HMC math + observatory tab itself landed at the W4→W5 boundary (2026-06-22).
accomplished: BEARDOWN Model 1 up as a local full-stack standalone site — EDA → leakage-safe data → frozen backbone → drop-in inference → Flask dashboard (tabs: EDA / experiment / model / data / glossary)
Leakage-safe data pipeline built: track-level vs naive split + BEARDOWN stratified seed-42 reproduction; clean log-mel @128 ⋈ 57-feature tabular; naive-vs-track gap captured as a result
Architecture vetted bit-faithful against the public INFO_510 repo (cfg_14: gated fusion, deterministic head, 573,450 params) — zero mechanism mismatch for the FORGE det-backbone + LLLA plan
Clean log-mel regeneration fixed the silent dirty-grey failure: train + inference now share one extract_mel recipe (validate r=1.0), so dropped songs no longer score as noise
Backbone frozen at clean-128 / batch-8: batch 32→8 lifted CV +0.086; frozen draw = val 0.7467 / test 0.700 / macro-F1 0.686 (573,450 params, bundle round-trips bit-exact)

Gap-to-0.766 fully diagnosed — early-stop, epochs/lr, representation, split, and resolution all ruled out; lever was batch size, residual is framework + run variance. Decision: freeze, don’t chase 0.766 (the ~0.71 wall is FORGE’s motivating example, not a bug)
Song drop-in inference verified end-to-end on wav + mp3: 30-s windows → mel + 57 feats → per-genre prob + MC-dropout σ; load_audio hardened (soundfile → librosa fallback → clear error)
7-file frozen bundle shipped (weights / arch / scaler / label_map / phi_train.npy / ggn_eig.npz / metrics) — phi_train + GGN eigendecomp pre-staged so the Bayesian head is plug-ready
ML usage / cost ledger built (_shared/usage.py): per-run compute.json → energy / carbon / $ with measured-vs-modeled tags; rolls up all 11 runs (~0.33 h wall, ~14.8 Wh modeled-TDP)

5.label: MVP Phase 1 — Phonon
planned: Standalone site: run sweeps, model lock, drop-in analysis
refactored: Behind schedule entering W5. Pivot: build phonon as a stripped-down / more basic design first — get model 2 standing on the standalone template, then deepen — rather than the full BEARDOWN-depth treatment up front.

Genre proved the full-stack template (EDA → data → frozen model → inference → dashboard); phonon copies the skeleton and fills only the three domain pieces (data adapter, EDA, features/model/config) to hit the “get it running” floor.

Still in flux across all three models: model 2 (phonon) and model 3 (ATLAS) are scaffold-only (skeleton repos, no data/runs yet), and the unified FORGE layout / metrics view is still being designed — the per-model dashboards will converge on one shared FORGE look in Phase 2.

Phonon absorbed the FORGE-layer generalization: rather than a stripped-down site, the phonon build hardened the shared observatory (τ grab-slider, 3-tier data source, independent CLI) so ATLAS inherits a template-stable layer — this is why the phonon work ran W5→W6.

accomplished.name: FORGE Bayesian core landed for genre (carry-over from W4): LLLA last-layer Laplace + HMC gold-standard sampler on the frozen head, plus the observatory tab (overview / posterior / model / τ-sweep / eigenspectrum / data-frac / report / HMC)
Headline finding wired into the FORGE report: most last-layer weight-directions are prior-led → model is data-limited, not capacity-limited (answers “can it go further, or is it noise-capped?”)

Phonon FORGE observatory built end-to-end on the DOS regression (51-bin, Chen et al. 2021 reproduction): forge.html dashboard + Flask server.py + forge_dashboard.py payload assembler, wrapping mk1/mk2/mk3 frozen backbones with an LLLA head
LLLA intercept fix for phonon: DOS baseline centering (ymean) lifted the regression head from R² ≈ −27 to ≈ 0.95 (PICP ≈ 0.95) on the template bundle
Phonon — data adapter + domain EDA + features/model/config filled into the skeleton (mk2 EMD backbone as the headline)

planned: Standalone site: run sweeps, model lock, drop-in analysis

ATLAS is not yet 'officially added' to the doc-site ecosystem, but the parallel model progress keeps the W6 Gantt floor on track — the FORGE observatory + LLLA/HMC layer is now template-stable (genre + phonon), so ATLAS is a data-adapter + config wrap, not new infrastructure.

accomplished.name: Phonon FORGE observatory finished: continuous data-limited verdict (γ = λ/(λ+τ) with %-confidence gauges), Last-Layer Model panel (W-map heatmap · σ-heatmap · all-1,632-posteriors bell grid · click-to-inspect prior-vs-posterior Gaussian), Optimization Frontier (RRM heat map + Pareto front), and independent forge_cli.py calculators (synth→fit→payload regenerates everything, nothing hard-coded)

HMC made full-stack: FIRE HMC VALIDATION button → real server-side sampler (Flask /api/forge/hmc, forge.hmc_run) → fire/progress animation → per-bin chain-trace + sample-histogram-with-Laplace-Gaussian overlay (validates the fast approximation the rest of the dashboard rides on). Synthetic-bundle fallback so it runs before real bundles exist
ATLAS Run-3 LLP / MSVtx models advancing in parallel (barrel/endcap ABCD, ABCDisCoTEC×DNCQN ablation harness on real data) — standalone-site integration into the FORGE template still pending
ATLAS — EDA + standalone-site skeleton (data adapter + domain EDA + features/model/config) fold-in

8.label: MVP Phase 2 — integrate + deploy (risk window opens)
planned: Tie together repos into official FORGE website
Move from localhost to external hosting
Final decisions on Bayesian tune options, look, dashboards
refactored: Deployment architecture DECIDED: 'host on my PC' — GitHub Pages serves the static apex (splash + floor), a Docker container on my own machine serves the app, and a Cloudflare Tunnel (Zero Trust Free) publishes it at genre.forge-observatory.com. $0/month, no PaaS.

Dev/publish split locked: native Flask localhost is the entire workbench (one server carries splash → floor → select → dashboard, smart port scan); Docker is the shipping container only — one command (publish_mk3.ps1) does engine → build → container → smoke (incl. ML-stack probe) → tunnel → push.

accomplished.name: Full stack BUILT and integrated — one Flask app serves the whole FORGE chain: splash → floor → BEARDOWN model-select → dashboard with Feature Stats (provenance), the τ-knob Observatory promoted to bay 02 (in-browser posterior recompute off cached eigen-projections, GGN spectrum, data-fraction sweep, gated HMC console), and the Drop Deck (song upload → MK1/MK2/MK3 verdict cards with ±σ)

Proof of concept DEPLOYED public with the BEARDOWN model — https://genre.forge-observatory.com live through the Cloudflare tunnel off my own hardware; apex splash/floor on Pages; container smoke-gated before every publish

Verified end-to-end from ANOTHER PC — a remote machine dropped a track through the public site and received all three family verdicts. First remote test exposed the serving image missing torch (pyproject documents the TF training tier; the serve path is torch) — fixed with an explicit CPU-torch image layer, and the publish gate now includes an ML-stack smoke so a hollow image can never ship again
Ops hardening en route: container host ports moved out of the dev 5000-range (5601/5602), HMC sampler env-gated OFF on the public face, Docker-engine cold-start + port-forensics probe scripts added

9.label: MVP Phase 2 — front-end restart + tutorial (risk window)
refactored: Write-up start DEFERRED to W10 by decision. The public proof-of-concept made the front end the binding constraint rather than the Bayesian core, so the week went to a UI/UX restart; the deployed BEARDOWN site stayed live and untouched throughout.
Design work moved into a NEW repo, FORGE_site_dev — stage C, flow / look / stub widgets only, no backend. forge-observatory remains the deploy repo and nothing shipped out of site-dev this week.

Interface flow collapsed: dash 1 (choose model) and dash 2 (choose Fidget / FORGE) merged into ONE screen — the holographic model-select deck. Path is now splash → deck → [FIDGET | FORGE] → main dash.
Product scope narrowed: ONE model per experiment is featured in the product (of the three built per family); the sibling models are discussed in the write-up instead of shipped.

Tutorial scope decided: Palmer Penguins — deliberately boring, well known, CC0 — built as a STANDALONE repo (forge-lite) to be folded into forge-observatory later rather than bolted onto the deploy repo mid-flight.
Drop Deck performance work PARKED by decision until the whole site is public: the triage is recorded and the deltas are scoped, but applying them now would churn a stack that is about to be rebuilt.

accomplished.name: FORGE contract formalized and published — the tiered artifact agreement an experiment must satisfy to be wrapped: Tier 0 statistical core (phi_train, y_train, likelihood family, tau config), Tier 1 fitted cache (LLLA head, GGN eigenbasis, capabilities array, metrics card), Tier 2 input-space adapters (backbone, scaler, label map), Tier 3 display artifacts (EDA stats). Governing principle: adapters end at φ, FORGE begins at φ. Added to this site as panels/contract.html with nav + router entries.

Gauges CALIBRATED against real bundles and locked (FORGE_gauge_LOCKIN_mk1.txt) — offline bench run with the experiments repo's own llla.py / hmc.py across 5 genre bundles (d ∈ {384, 512, 768}, N=700, C=10): G1 = epistemic share % (BALD mutual-information fraction, observed 20–52%, and it separates MK1/MK3 from MK2), G2 = gain at 2× data %, G3 = LLLA↔HMC fidelity 1−TV (42–46% at τ*, which is what makes RUN FULL HMC a meaningful button rather than decoration), G4 = focus = 100 − participation ratio of dσ/dφ. Raw data-determined direction share (0.9–2.1%) proved ungaugeable on a linear dial and was demoted to the eigenspectrum headline; τ knob locked to the repo's own scale, τ = 10^k · λmax, k ∈ [−4, 0], default −2.

The four tenets named and mapped one-to-one onto the four gauges: PROVENANCE (what went into the model), POSTERIOR (how sure is it, really), ATTRIBUTION (why did it say that), GENEALOGY (is this one better than the last one). Accuracy is deliberately NOT a gauge — it is the number you already had — and there is no fifth gauge averaging the other four, because 'better' is a trade with terms, not a scalar.

FORGE main-dash wireframe locked: model-name box plus the four tenet gauges across the top; user-alert / model-data / graph-map box at middle-left; graph bay with ◀▶ paging and an expand popup at middle-right; user controls, RUN FULL HMC and GENERATE AUDIT (new tab, downloadable) along the bottom. Instrument aesthetic fixed: black / grey chassis so the gauge colors carry, dials reading as analog meters plus a segmented-LED arc with a 7-segment digital readout.

Model-select deck BUILT — the HELIX holographic desktop reworked into FORGE's single select screen (Three.js, SOLAR palette, all HELIX references stripped): four tall glass model plates over a green-cathode CRT that holds the help rows and types deck-log facts, brand and BACK TO SPLASH tiles, zoom key and orientation gizmo, standard view pinned at 65% / EL +17°. Hover snaps a plate front and charges the center bulb to that model's accent, projecting the beam onto it; click opens [FIDGET | FORGE]; keys 1–4 and ?model= deep links ride the same path. Boot sequence ~11.8 s (dive on the flame → crane over the flat disk → tiers pop → beam prints 29 elements by bearing → control-demo outro that teaches the mouse); any input skips it and reduced-motion lands straight on the finished deck.

Splash REBUILT across three passes (mk17 → mk19) down to a single-strike ignition: the full brand lockup (flame + F·O·R·G·E + POSTERIOR OBSERVATORY) drawn large and central, a constant ember field floating up like inverted snow, a blacksmith-hammer strike key, brighter glow on hover and sparks on click. Two ignition behaviors ship behind IGNITE_MODE — 'flare' (default, ~1.4 s: sparks → catch → white-out → cross to the deck) and 'burn' (the 2 s burn-through that eats the lockup and reveals the P(θ|D) card underneath).
FORGE hype video produced — short promo cut for the project.

forge-lite BUILT as the tutorial experiment: Palmer Penguins end to end — a click-through walk of the four tenets, then the user builds their own model by live backend retrain inside a ~5-minute cap, then FORGE has to show something real about what they built. Genealogy arc mk1 → mk2 → mk3 → mk3-blind → mk3-geo, with mk3-blind (bill length withheld) parked deliberately on genuine irreducible uncertainty: 0.816 three-class accuracy, Gentoo recall holding at 1.000 while Chinstrap recall falls to 0.381 — so the posterior tenet has something to say instead of a wall of 0.99s.

Drop Deck performance triaged and recorded (FORGE_perf_pass_RECORD_jul20.txt, bench_predict_mk2.py, bench_results.json): baseline 48 MB track = 14.4 s total (~7 s librosa features + ~6.8 s MC forwards). Bundle-reload hypothesis acquitted at 35 ms; the mk3 batch-1 MC loop confirmed as the single biggest block at 5.74 s (40%); mk1 and mk2 confirmed recomputing identical features; cold import 1.3–2.5 s per boot. Delta mk1 (gunicorn gthread, [predict] timers, edge cache, locks) delivered unapplied; mk2 (batched MC + shared features, target ~8–10 s) and mk3 (progressive cards) scoped for after the site is up.

Dev ergonomics: boot_site_mk1.ps1 serves the site-dev repo — scans 8000–8020 on loopback, prints the local address, auto-opens the browser, logs live requests, cleans up on Ctrl+C (-Port / -NoOpen switches; README gained a Boot section with the Unblock-File ritual and a manual fallback).
